title: Finite model-category axioms transported by a categorical equivalence
statement: Use small colimits as defined in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; limits are the dual universal notion. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be ordinary categories and let $E:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$ be an equivalence. Suppose $\mathcal D$ has classes $\mathrm{Cof},\mathrm{Fib},W$ of arrows satisfying these axioms: finite limits and finite colimits exist; $W$ satisfies two-out-of-three; all three classes are closed under retracts of arrows; a member of $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$ has the left lifting property against every member of $\mathrm{Fib}$, and a member of $\mathrm{Cof}$ has the left lifting property against every member of $\mathrm{Fib}\cap W$; and every arrow factors both as a member of $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$ followed by a member of $\mathrm{Fib}$ and as a member of $\mathrm{Cof}$ followed by a member of $\mathrm{Fib}\cap W$. Here an arrow $i:A\to B$ has the left lifting property against $p:X\to Y$ if for every $a:A\to X$, $b:B\to Y$ with $pa=bi$ there is $d:B\to X$ with $di=a$ and $pd=b$; a retract of arrows is a retract in the category whose objects are arrows and whose morphisms are commutative squares. Give $\mathcal C$ the inverse-image classes under $E$. These classes satisfy all the same axioms on $\mathcal C$, including the two factorizations and both lifting assertions.
